maintainer_decisions.question: A StaticHoursProfile carries one tz and seconds-since-local-midnight rules. Ten shapes open at 17:00 America/Chicago and close at a fixed wall-clock instant in London, Singapore, Shanghai, Hong Kong or Tokyo. How is that represented?
maintainer_decisions.recommendation: Adopt Option G — keep tz America::Chicago, ship two StaticHoursProfile values per key, select with reference_delta_seconds. U-8's premise is FALSE: four genuine cross-zone selectors already ship (ice_endex, ice_abu_dhabi, b3, bmv), ice_abu_dhabi.rs is the exact mirror of this proposal, and MarketHoursKey::EurexFixedIncome is the key-side precedent whose module already writes down the central argument. Zero API change, zero serde change, no migration, no existing key's golden rows move, and AGENTS.md already anticipates it. The single-grid alternative costs 20 hours a year of false-closed or false-open EXECUTABLE window for the London-anchored shapes and an hour wrong on 35-65% of weekdays for the Asian anchors, and AGENTS.md ranks executable-window gaps highest. SCOPE the answer to the ten shapes carrying CME's Friday-16:00 / Sunday-17:00 CT weekly close: it is NOT exact for the two 24/7 crypto BTIC shapes (verdict N1). Do not spend the mechanism on America/New_York-anchored shapes, which are exactly representable in Chicago local seconds.

maintainer_decisions.question: CME's own TAS eligibility workbook has exactly six tabs and its single Energy TAS sheet covers CLT MCT NGT HHT 7FT TAS TTS together. This plan proposes ten TAS keys and five TAM keys. Is that right?
maintainer_decisions.recommendation: Keep the ten TAS and five TAM keys, decided on family semantics and history rather than on the envelope, which is what handoff §3.3 asks for. Metals TAS splits five ways (five closes, launches spanning 2010-2018, copper's and palladium's coincident 12:00 on different exchanges and groups — the globex_mini_grains precedent governs). Energy TAS and gasoil TAS split because 7FT's close differs in EVERY sourced era. DO NOT split rows 10/22 (CLT/HOT/RBT/BZT/BBT vs NGT/NNT): they differ only by a Pre-Open second the crate does not encode and a one-to-two-minute 2011-2012 stagger, never by an executable boundary. Three energy TAM keys, not one: they differ by one constant each under Option G, and AGENTS.md's 'a venue that merely coincides with another still gets its own named profile so a future divergence is a one-line edit' applies directly to three different city closes.

maintainer_decisions.question: Does 'pending all relevant CFTC regulatory review periods' defeat an effective day? The handoff rates TACO's 2018 launch High while U-19 rejects two 2019 days partly because they carry 'pending'. Those cannot both stand, and the clause appears on most CME launch and eligibility documents in this handoff.
maintainer_decisions.recommendation: A conditional clause on a day now in the PAST, whose occurrence is independently witnessed by a post-effective artifact in the operator's own channel, is DISCHARGED and the row is encodable — with the discharge recorded beside the row. The crate already does exactly this: livestock.rs keys 2016-02-29 to SER-7591 despite its 'pending CFTC review' clause, discharged by a 2016-03-03 fact card and a 2016-03-11 spec page. Two supports: CME publishes UNCONDITIONAL days in the same weekly channel (the 2021-06-21 halt-removal item has no clause), so the clause is applied selectively to CFTC-self-certified listings and is not boilerplate to be read past; and LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES forbids encoding a FUTURE date contingent on a filing, not a past witnessed day. U-19 stays rejected for a DIFFERENT reason — two documents name two different days, which is a conflict, and the sourced-intersection convention has nothing to intersect when the disputed thing is a launch day. Write the adjudication once, in AGENTS.md beside LAW-NO-FABRICATED-DATES, and cite it from every row that relies on it; that is a law edit and belongs in its own PR.

maintainer_decisions.question: Does a labelled closed@ event in /services/trading-hours-by-product promote a marker instant to a session close? globex_gold_tam and globex_copper_tam rest SOLELY on it, and CME's prose for both gives only a marker CALCULATION window — while U-16 narrowed the rule in the opposite direction for TACO's Saturday rows.
maintainer_decisions.recommendation: Yes for GCD and HGF, on a narrowed rule that resolves both cases consistently: a venue feed's own labelled close/halt event is session language EXCEPT where the operator's own prose contradicts it. A marker calculation window is SILENT about the session, not contrary to it; the same feed vocabulary is accepted without argument for the five TAM shapes whose FAQ states the close in session language; and withholding would leave two families unmapped on a distinction the operator itself does not draw (its eligibility workbook's Metals TAM sheet lists exactly these two roots beside the energy ones). LAW-SESSION-NOT-EXPIRY's own text already admits 'a venue feed's own close/halt event'; the narrowing only adds the contradiction carve-out, and TACO's Saturday rows are its worked example — note they are a full open+close PAIR, not the close/halt event the law names, which is an independent reason to reject them. Record the narrowing in AGENTS.md in its own commit; it does not belong in a key's doc comment. If the answer is no, drop PR 12 and record GCD/HGF in unsupported-families.md naming the two closed@ values so the next reader does not re-derive them.

maintainer_decisions.question: Energy TAS: one era from the floor at 16:15/16:45 with RA1104-4's stagger recorded beside the table, or two eras with the 16:17/16:47 intersection?
maintainer_decisions.recommendation: Two eras. RA1104-4 is an unconditional dated primary in session language, and the crate's convention is to encode a dated row even when it touches only order-entry — both metals TAS order-entry rows do exactly that. Either way, do not split the key: the executable window is identical for every root in every sourced era.

maintainer_decisions.question: MCT (U-0a): map on published-group identity, or leave unmapped? Re-derive every tally from the MERGED ledger; never resolve a count conflict by picking a side. PR 1's fences turn that from a review habit into a red test.
